raw_case_text:
A 15-year-old previously healthy girl came to our hospital because of history of 7 days duration of high-grade fever. She also had complaints of arthralgia, back pain, and myalgia. On examination, she was febrile, and there were no rashes, petechiae, hematuria, hematemesis, or hemoptysis. The blood pressure was 120/80 mmHg, pulse rate 102 beats/min, respiratory rate 18 breaths/min, and temperature was 38.4 C by axilla. Cardiovascular and respiratory system revealed no significant abnormality. Hematology revealed pancytopenia with a hemoglobin level of 8.8 g/dL, leukocyte count 1510/mm3 with differential count of 43.1% neutrophils, 47% lymphocytes, 4.6% monocytes, and 4.6% eosinophils, and platelets were 19,000/mm3. Serum bilirubin was 1.03 mg/dL, alanine aminotransferase 294 IU/L, aspartate aminotransferase 145 IU/L, and lactate dehydrogenase was 461 IU/L. Renal function tests, electrolytes, chest X-ray, and electrocardiogram were within normal limit. NS1 antigen and IgM antibodies were positive for dengue virus. She tested negative for malaria, HIV, hepatitis B surface antigen, hepatitis C virus, and chikungunya. Urine analysis was sterile. Ultrasonography showed mild bilateral pleural effusion, mild ascites, mild hepatomegaly, and marginal splenomegaly. The serum triglyceride level was 377 mg/dL, serum ferritin >2000 ng/ml, and plasma D-dimer was high. Bone marrow aspiration showed mild hypocellular marrow with increase in macrophages and monocytes activity. Few macrophages were seen with engulfed platelets and neutrophils within it.
The diagnosis of DF with hemophagocytic syndrome was confirmed by evidence of fever with positive serological tests, hypertriglyceridemia, hyperferritinemia, splenomegaly, and bone marrow hemophagocytes. She was treated with intravenous fluids and antipyretics. We discharged her on the 10th day in hemodynamically stable and afebrile condition with normal hematological parameters.

subjective.chief_complaint: A 15-year-old female presenting with a 7-day history of high-grade fever, arthralgia, back pain, and myalgia.
subjective.history_of_present_illness: A 15-year-old previously healthy female presented with a 7-day history of high-grade fever accompanied by arthralgia, back pain, and generalized myalgia. She had no history of rash, petechiae, hematuria, hematemesis, or hemoptysis.
subjective.past_medical_history: Previously healthy with no prior medical illnesses.
subjective.review_of_systems: Positive for fever, arthralgias, back pain, and myalgias. Negative for rash, petechiae, hematuria, hematemesis, or hemoptysis. Medications and allergies: null.

objective.physical_examination: Temperature: 38.4 C (axillary), blood pressure: 120/80 mmHg, pulse rate: 102 beats/min, respiratory rate: 18 breaths/min. Febrile. No rashes, petechiae, or ecchymoses. Cardiovascular and respiratory system examinations revealed no significant abnormalities.
objective.routine_investigations: Hemoglobin: 8.8 g/dL, leukocyte count: 1,510/mm3 (differential: 43.1% neutrophils, 47% lymphocytes, 4.6% monocytes, 4.6% eosinophils), platelets: 19,000/mm3, demonstrating pancytopenia. Serum bilirubin: 1.03 mg/dL, ALT: 294 IU/L, AST: 145 IU/L, LDH: 461 IU/L. Serum triglycerides: 377 mg/dL, serum ferritin: >2,000 ng/mL, plasma D-dimer: high. Renal function tests and electrolytes: Within normal limits. Urinalysis: Sterile. Serological tests for malaria, HIV, HBsAg, HCV, and chikungunya were negative. Chest X-ray and ECG: Within normal limits. Abdominal ultrasonography: Mild bilateral pleural effusion, mild ascites, mild hepatomegaly, and marginal splenomegaly.
objective.advanced_workup: Bone marrow aspiration: Mild hypocellular marrow with increased macrophage and monocyte activity; macrophages demonstrating hemophagocytosis with engulfed platelets and neutrophils.

assessment_and_plan.assessment_and_confirmation:
Definitive diagnosis: Dengue fever complicated by secondary hemophagocytic lymphohistiocytosis / hemophagocytic syndrome (HLH), confirmed by fever, splenomegaly, pancytopenia, hypertriglyceridemia, hyperferritinemia, and bone marrow hemophagocytosis. Diagnostic confirmation: Positive dengue virus NS1 antigen and IgM antibodies; negative tests for malaria, HIV, HBV, HCV, and chikungunya.
Plan & Outcome: Treated supportively with intravenous fluids and antipyretics. Discharged on hospital day 10 in hemodynamically stable, afebrile condition with normal hematological parameters.
